$schema-note: The flake catalogue the merge-queue steward (.github/scripts/merge-queue-steward.py) re-queues on.
Doc: src/MeshWeaver.Documentation/Data/Architecture/MergeQueue.md (Doc/Architecture/MergeQueue).
An entry is a TEMPORARY, EVIDENCE-BEARING allowance for one known race while its root cause is
fixed — never a permanent tolerance. Every field is required and the steward's loader refuses
the file (and `MergeQueueStewardGuard` reds the build) when one is missing or malformed:
id                a short stable handle, unique in this file
assertionPattern  a regex over the failure MESSAGE + STACK TRACE — never over the test name.
It must be specific to the defect (a bare 'timed out' is not evidence);
a pattern that matches the empty string is refused.
testName          informational: the fully-qualified test the assertion belongs to
issue             the GitHub issue tracking the root cause (https://github.com/Systemorph/<repo>/issues/N)
evidence          run URLs: at least one FAILING run showing the assertion, ideally beside a
PASSING run of the same tree — the control arm (Doc/Architecture/ReadingCiSignals)
addedOn / expires ISO dates; expires is at most 30 days after addedOn. An expired entry is
inert (the steward treats it as uncatalogued) AND reds the guard until it is
deleted or renewed with fresh evidence.
addedBy           who vouches for the evidence
Seeded EMPTY on 2026-09-02 after mining the 700 Build-and-Test runs since the queue was first
enabled (2026-08-30, 83 failures). Nothing met the bar: the repeated signatures belonged to
MeshWeaver.Hosting.Monolith.Test, which has since moved to MeshWeaver.Plugins; the six-times
TestTimeoutLiteralRatchetGuard red was the queue doing its job (two PRs each moved a ratchet
count — a real semantic conflict, not a flake); and every remaining candidate was a single
occurrence or had its subject changed after the failing runs.
